newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Gazprom, govt say reach agreement on debt.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Gazprom, govt say reach agreement on debt.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov and Gazprom head Rem Vyakhirev have found a solution to the gas monopoly's debts problems, Nemtsov's press secretary and a Gazprom official said on Monday.
Neither source provided any further details.
The RAO Gazprom spokesman said Vyakhirev would hold a press conference on Tuesday, when he would be able to address the question of the company's debts.

Gazprom debts totalled 14.8 trillion roubles ($2.6 billion), 50 percent more than government budget arrears to Russian workers, Nemtsov said during an interview on Russia's Itogi news programme late on Sunday.
Gazprom has said that debts owed to it for gas already supplied stood at 64 trillion roubles as of February 1.
Vyakhirev last week attacked the finance ministry and the International Monetary Fund for acting in the interests of foreign oil and gas companies which wanted to see the giant company split up.
Nemtsov said that the government wanted to preserve Gazprom as a single company, but that the government's share in the company must be managed appropriately.
The government owns 40 percent of Gazprom shares, but handed 35 percent of shares over to Vyakhirev's management.
Privatisation minister Alfred Kokh said on Thursday that Vyakhirev's management of the 35 percent share may be looked at following his criticism of the government.
Vyakhirev also said last week that the amount of fines on overdue Gazprom payments to the budget for supplies delivered to budget-financed organisations should be reduced.
